q01:
We're ahead of pace to date, but if nothing changes the program lands at 57329 doors on Election Day, 3303 short of the 60632 goal.
- Program pace to date (Sep 21 to Oct 18): 33503 doors vs a goal to date of 32431, 103.3% of goal [table:v_office_pace_total]
- Projection: 57329 doors, 94.6% of goal, projected_vs_goal -3303 [table:v_office_pace_total]
- By office: Northside projects 23583 (+908, 104%); Harbor 19150 (-1007, 95%); Eastgate 14596 (-3204, 82%) [table:v_office_pace]
- Eastgate is also behind pace to date at 89.3%; Harbor is at 105.3% and Northside at 112.5% [table:v_office_pace]
- Method: doors to date plus the last 7 days' average daily doors (1489.1 program-wide) times the 16 knocking days left; an office misses goal when its projection is below its total goal [doc:program-plan#pace-and-projection]
q03:
Eastgate needs 4.4 more shifts a day, Harbor 1.3 more, and Northside none; the program as a whole needs 4.1 more.
- Eastgate: 12.6 shifts a day needed vs 8.3 a day in the last 7 days (Oct 12 to 18), so 4.4 extra [table:v_office_pace]
- Harbor: 11.1 needed vs 9.9, so 1.3 extra [table:v_office_pace]
- Northside: 10.1 needed vs 11.1, so 0 extra [table:v_office_pace]
- Program total: 33.3 needed vs 29.3, so 4.1 extra [table:v_office_pace_total]
- Based on 16 knocking days left and last 7 days' doors per shift (45.9 Eastgate, 49.4 Harbor, 55.7 Northside, 50.8 program) [table:v_office_pace]
q05:
Ask the client for more doors: at our current pace we'll knock more doors than the untouched turf we have left, and new turf beats a second pass.
- Capacity for the rest of the program: 1489.1 average daily doors (last 7 days, Oct 12 to 18) x 16 knocking days left [table:v_office_pace_total]
- Untouched doors left in our turf: 10393 of 41853 turf doors [table:v_office_pace_total]
- We're also projected to miss goal by 3303 doors (57329 vs 60632) [table:v_office_pace_total]
- Rule: when capacity is larger than untouched doors, ask the client for more doors first; a second pass on not-home doors is the fallback because it contacts voters at roughly half the first-pass rate [doc:program-plan#more-doors-or-a-second-pass]
q07:
The client's report counts attempts before QC rollbacks, while our dashboard counts doors once per day with rollbacks removed; on Oct 12 that gap was 203 program-wide, mostly 142 rolled-back attempts in Eastgate.
- Program, Oct 12: client sheet 1484 vs our 1281 doors, a gap of 203: 142 rolled-back attempts plus 61 repeat attempts [table:v_daily_doors_total]
- Eastgate: 498 reported vs 342 doors, gap 156 = 142 rolled back + 14 repeat attempts [table:v_daily_doors]
- Harbor: 428 vs 406, gap 22, all repeat attempts [table:v_daily_doors]
- Northside: 558 vs 533, gap 25, all repeat attempts [table:v_daily_doors]
- Why: the client report is pulled at the end of each day before any QC rollback; the gap is repeat attempts at the same door plus attempts later rolled back, and a large gap almost always means a rollback [doc:counting-doors#why-the-client-s-numbers-differ-from-ours]
q09:
Contact rates are up program-wide this week, rising in Northside and Harbor but falling in Eastgate.
- Program: 27.9% this week (Oct 12 to 18) vs 26.9% last week (Oct 5 to 11) [table:v_contact_rates_total]
- Northside: up to 30.1% from 26.4% [table:v_contact_rates]
- Harbor: up to 27.3% from 26.1% [table:v_contact_rates]
- Eastgate: down to 25% from 28.8% [table:v_contact_rates]
- Contact rate is contacts (knocks marked canvassed) divided by doors for the same office and period [doc:counting-doors#contacts-and-contact-rate]
q11:
This week (Oct 12 to 18) four canvassers had flash knocking or householding flags; the repeat problem is one person, Dorian Pratt in Eastgate, not a whole office.
- Dorian Pratt (Eastgate): 3 householding flags, on Oct 13 (QC031, reviewed), Oct 17 (QC034, open) and Oct 18 (QC035, open) [table:v_qc_flags_detail]
- Jalen Ortiz (Eastgate): 1 flash knocking flag on Oct 12 (QC030, reviewed), 142 knocks, whole shift rolled back [table:v_qc_flags_detail]
- Priya Nandakumar (Harbor): 1 flash knocking flag on Oct 18 (QC036, open), 13 consecutive knocks a median 12 s apart [table:v_qc_flags_detail]
- Tomas Reyes (Northside): 1 householding flag on Oct 14 (QC032, reviewed) [table:v_qc_flags_detail]
- Two or more householding or flash knocking flags in one week for the same canvasser go to the field director, so Dorian Pratt's should be escalated; open flags need a field lead conversation before the next shift [doc:qc-rules#what-happens-after-a-flag]
q13:
QC is getting better program-wide, falling from 4.3 to 3.4 flags per 100 shifts this week; Harbor improved the most, Northside improved too, and Eastgate got worse.
- Program: 8.1 (Sep 21 week), 6.1 (Sep 28), 4.3 (last week, Oct 5 to 11), 3.4 (this week, Oct 12 to 18) flags per 100 shifts [table:v_qc_weekly_total]
- Harbor: 6.2 last week to 1.4 this week [table:v_qc_weekly]
- Northside: 3 to 1.3 [table:v_qc_weekly]
- Eastgate: 3.8 to 8.6, with 5 flags on 58 shifts this week [table:v_qc_weekly]
- The QC rate is flags per 100 GOTV shifts per office per week; trends use the rate, not raw flag counts, because shifts grow during the program [doc:qc-rules#qc-rate]

x04:
Flash knocking is recording doors faster than a person can walk to them and knock; a shift is flagged when 10 or more consecutive knocks are recorded less than 30 seconds apart.
- Threshold: 10 or more consecutive knocks under 30 seconds apart [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
- Confirmed flash knocking is rolled back: those knocks no longer count as doors or contacts, and a whole shift recorded this way is rolled back in full [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
- Rolled-back knocks stay in the data marked rolled back, and rollbacks never change a client report already sent [doc:counting-doors#rollbacks]
- An open flag needs a field lead conversation before the canvasser's next shift; two or more in one week go to the field director [doc:qc-rules#what-happens-after-a-flag]
